headline: Record quarter as new streams meet strong metal prices
summary_short: Royal Gold's first quarter (ended March 31, 2026) delivered record revenue of $469.1 million, up 142.5% y/y, with net income of $281.1 million ($3.30 diluted EPS) up 147.7% y/y, driven by the 2025 Sandstorm/Horizon and Kansanshi additions layering onto sharply higher gold, silver and copper prices.
summary_long: Revenue rose to $469.1M (71% gold, 16% silver, 10% copper) on higher realized metal prices ($4,873/oz gold vs $2,860), new Kansanshi and Sandstorm/Horizon interests, and higher sales at Andacollo, Xavantina and Rainy River, partly offset by lower Mount Milligan sales. Costs rose on the larger asset base but trailed revenue growth, lifting operating income 141.3% and net income 147.7%. Operating cash flow rose 115.3% to $293.6M. The company repaid $300M of revolving-credit debt this quarter (a further $75M post-quarter), is tracking within its March 2026 full-year sales-volume, DD&A and tax-rate guidance, and post-quarter added a $600M credit accordion and a $500M buyback authorization. Dividend $0.475/share, up 6% y/y.

drivers.explanation: Higher average gold, silver and copper prices; new Kansanshi and Sandstorm/Horizon revenue; higher gold sales at Andacollo, Xavantina and Rainy River; partly offset by lower Mount Milligan sales.
Revenue grew $275.7M while total costs and expenses (cost of sales, G&A, DD&A) grew only $101.7M, on higher payments for stream deliveries and depletion from the new interests.
Tracked the operating-income gain plus a DD&A add-back that rose to $90.9M from $33.0M as depletion from Kansanshi and Sandstorm/Horizon layered onto the base.
Adjusted EBITDA rose to $391.0M from $159.2M; margin expanded to 83% from 82% as revenue outgrew the largely fixed corporate cost base.
Primarily attributable to higher revenue and a $14.1M gain on the sale of Highlander shares, partially offset by higher cost of sales, depletion, interest expense and income tax expense.
Diluted share count rose to 85.0M from 65.8M following 2025 Sandstorm/Horizon share issuance, so per-share growth (91.9%) trailed net income growth (147.7%).
Primarily due to $198.1M higher net cash proceeds from stream and royalty interests, partially offset by higher income tax, G&A and interest payments.
Financing activities used $327.2M (mostly $300.0M of debt repayment and higher dividend payments), which outweighed the record operating cash inflow versus the year-ago balance.
Repaid $300 million on the revolving credit facility during the quarter; a further $75 million was repaid after quarter-end, reducing the drawn amount to $525 million.
Retained-earnings growth from record net income combined with the 2025 Sandstorm/Horizon share issuance (diluted share count nearly doubled y/y), which was not fully offset by dividends paid.

Record revenue, operating cash flow and net income from the 2025 Sandstorm/Horizon and Kansanshi additions meeting strong metal prices; company is tracking within its March 2026 full-year guidance and added a buyback and credit-facility accordion post-quarter.
